name: Non-profit learning platform
note: An online learning platform for kids, built for a non-profit: interactive math exercises, a teacher dashboard and read-only parent access, on serverless infrastructure.
problem: The founder had a clear vision and a budget that was a fraction of what most agencies would quote. Cutting features was the obvious answer; prioritising differently was the better one.

approach.title: Three launch features
approach.text: Only what mattered for launch went in. Community, gamification, advanced analytics and notifications went onto a post-launch list.

approach.title: Learning first
approach.text: Interactive math exercises kids can complete on their own. If this did not work well, nothing else mattered.

approach.title: Teacher dashboard
approach.text: Simple progress tracking: who completed what, and where they struggled.

approach.title: Parent access
approach.text: A read-only view of their child’s progress. No editing, no complex permissions.

approach.title: Serverless and simple auth
approach.text: Resources scale with usage, and secure email and password sign-in saved about a week of work.

results.label: a month for the first 500 users
lower infrastructure cost than traditional hosting
launch, with a foundation that did not need rebuilding

features: Serverless infrastructure that scales with usage
